question: In which order does breadth-first search visit the nodes if it starts at A and takes neighbours in alphabetical order? How would depth-first search from A differ?
reference_answer: Edges: A-B, A-C, A-E, B-D, B-F, C-G, E-F. BFS uses a FIFO queue: visit A, enqueue its neighbours B, C, E (distance 1); dequeue B -> enqueue D, F; dequeue C -> enqueue G; dequeue E (its neighbour F is already discovered); then D, F, G (distance 2). BFS order: A, B, C, E, D, F, G. DFS (stack / recursion, going as deep as possible before backtracking): A -> B -> D (dead end, back to B) -> F -> E (via the bottom edge F-E) -> back up to A -> C -> G. DFS order: A, B, D, F, E, C, G.
